region: Braunschweig / Bad Harzburg, Lower Saxony (the repo's home region)
judged_by: manual curation from local route knowledge, 2026-09 (issue #4)
notes: Coordinates are [lon, lat]-order landmarks shared with scripts/compare_backends.py and the live tests.
Expectations encode what a rider familiar with each corridor judges a good engine route to look like;
they are plausibility envelopes, not golden geometries. Missing data never fails a check -- it is
reported as skipped (unknown must stay unknown, see docs/enrichment.md and docs/scoring-and-exports.md).

cases.title: Braunschweig Hbf -> Bürgerpark (city hop)
cases.rationale: Straight line is ~1.0 km through a dense, well-tagged city grid; a good city route is a short street-level hop, almost entirely hard-surfaced, with only marginal ascent.

cases.title: Braunschweig Hbf -> Burg Dankwarderode / Domplatz (historic centre)
cases.rationale: The castle-square area around the Burg and Dom is famously cobbled; a route whose surface profile has zero masonry here indicates missing enrichment data or a bad match, not a genuinely smooth approach. Overall the old town remains hard-surfaced (paved + masonry dominate).

cases.title: Braunschweig Hbf -> Schloss Wolfenbüttel (flat valley tour)
cases.rationale: ~11.2 km straight line down the Oker valley; real routes run 12-18 km along valley paths and quiet roads. The valley is gentle: a credible touring route does not accumulate hundreds of metres of climbing.

cases.title: Bad Harzburg Bhf -> Braunlage Marktplatz (Harz plateau climb)
cases.rationale: The inverse case: ~18 km straight line but the towns sit at very different elevations, so every credible route climbs onto the Harz plateau. A candidate reporting less than ~250 m ascent here has broken or missing elevation data -- flagged, not silently rewarded (ascent is an expectation, never a bonus).

cases.title: Braunschweig Hbf -> Riddagshausen Klosterkirche (Oker path leisure ride)
cases.rationale: ~5.0 km straight line; the natural ride follows the Oker river paths southeast through the Riddagshausen nature reserve, so some unpaved share (compacted/soft/loose) is a hallmark of the expected route, and masonry should stay marginal.
